latin: Qui ordinem hebraicae linguae profunde et radicaliter tenuerit, atque illum proportionabiliter in scientiis seruare nouerit, cuiuscunque scibilis perfecte inueniendi_normam et regulam habebit.
latin_note: Farmer records a variant reading between printings: '1486 linguae profundae | 1487 lingue profunde' (farmer1998:21104).
translation: Whoever has grasped the order of the Hebrew language deeply and at its root, and knows how to preserve it proportionally in the sciences, will have the norm and rule for perfectly finding whatever is knowable.
translation_note: 'radicaliter' = 'at the root', i.e. a foundational grasp. 'proportionabiliter' = 'proportionally', by analogical extension of Hebrew's grammatical order to the sciences generally. 'scibilis' = 'of the knowable', that which can be known.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-swarm-batch3, from Latin at farmer1998:21095
doctrine: Thesis 3>55 claims that a deep, foundational grasp of the order of the Hebrew language, applied proportionally to the sciences, yields the norm and rule for perfectly discovering any knowable thing (farmer1998:21095). Farmer's note connects the thesis to 'the correlative foundations of Pico's revolutio alphabetariae', referring to his own discussion, and directs the reader also to the cluster of theses gathered at his note to 28.33 (paraphrase; farmer1998:21169).
context: Farmer's cross-reference apparatus ties the thesis to 11>2, Pico's fourfold division of speculative Kabbala including the 'alphabetariae revolutio' (farmer1998:26383), and to 3>56, on a third kind of distinction Pico calls 'inadequationis' (farmer1998:21181). Farmer's own note additionally directs the reader to the theses cross-referenced at 28.33 (paraphrase; farmer1998:21169), namely 28.47, 2>80, and 9>22.
reception: Mandosio quotes the thesis's Latin directly alongside 28.33 and 9>22 in a discussion of Pico's views on Hebrew and combinatorial method (mandosio2012:474). A German study of Pico's kabbalistic paradigm notes the thesis in connection with the concepts of 'Cabala practica' and 'Kawwanah', pointing to Wirszubski's discussion at pp. 140-144 and 147-148 (paraphrase; kabbalah_paradigma:2240).
historiography: Wirszubski treats the thesis with explicit caution: "Unless I am mistaken, Kabbala was also in Pico's mind when he wrote the fifty-fifth thesis of the Conclusiones paradoxae" (wirszubski1989:9650) — a hedge that marks this 'paradoxical' (non-Cabalistic-section) thesis as one whose Kabbalistic content is inferred rather than asserted outright by the section heading.

quotations.text: Unless I am mistaken, Kabbala was also in Pico's mind when he wrote the fifty-fifth thesis of the Conclusiones paradoxae

not_established: The precise relationship between the thesis's 'proportionabiliter' method and the specific technique of the revolutio alphabetariae, beyond Farmer's cross-reference, is not spelled out further in the sources consulted.
